2. The short facts of the petitioner's case is that the petitioner a citizen of Bangladesh and that the petitioner purchased House No. E/N/5 at Feroj Shah Housing Estate, under Mouza North Pahartali, Police Station Double-mooring, District-Chittagong vide Kabala No. 4033 dated 23-2-1980 Registered on 11-03-1980 from its real owner Mosammat Khurshida Begum wife of Syed Jahur Ahmad on PS Plot No. 1200 under PS Khatian No. 408 (Old) 4 (New) and Plot No. 1003 under DP Khatian No. 4 and present Municipal Holding No. 1388 measuring an area of 03 chatak along with boundary wall electric meter and water line. The said house originally belonged to the Government of erstwhile East Pakistan and the said authority allotted the house to one Syed Zahoor Ahmed Rezvi under Registered Agreement dated 18-5-1960 who acquired right, title and ownership of the house in accordance with clause 3 of the Agreement. The said Syed Jahoor Ahmed Rezvi executed a General Power of Attorney in favour of his wife Khursheda Begum daughter of Duda Miah of Village Mehar PS Chandina, District-Comilla giving her all powers including sell, mortgage and for creating charges. Thereafter Syed Jahoor Ahmed Rezvi died issueless and his wife sold the house to the petitioner. After purchase the vendor handed over vacant possession of the house to the petitioner and the petitioner started living there with her family. She resided in the house till September, 1980. Her husband in the meantime got allotment of a house from Bangladesh Jute Mills Corporation as he was an officer and the petitioner, sifted to that house by letting out this house on rent to one Abdul Halim. After Abdul Hajjm she let out the house to one Kalu Meah conractor and when Kalu Meah defaulted to pay rent she filed Complaint Case No. 48 of 1981 with the Pahartali Ward Office under the Chittagong Municipal Corporation. During the pendency of the case Kalu Meah appeared in the arbitration Council who gave a Judgment in this respect. 

 5. During the time BS Khatian was prepared and the house was shown in the list of abandoned property and she applied to the authority to restore her possession. The respondent No. 4 vide Memo No. 939 dated 12-2-1990 advised the petitioner to move to Court of Settlement. The petitioner filed Case No. 438 of 1992 before the 2nd Court of Settlement, Dhaka and vide order dated 13-3-1996 the court of settlement found that the house has rightly been excluded from the list of abandoned property. 

 7. Mr Syed Mokaddes Ali the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that the original allottee Syed Jahoor Ahmed Rezvi obtained allotment of the property from the Government of the then East Pakistan vide Registered deed dated 18-5-1960 (Annexure-'B' to the writ petition). The said Syed Jahoor Ahmed Rezvi executed a power of attorney in favour of his wife Most. Khursheeda Begum on 5-10-1973 giving her all powers including sale, transfer of the property (Annexure-'C' to the writ petition) the said Syed Jahoor Ahmed Razvi died intestate issueless and his wife Mst Khursheeda Begum sold out the house in favour of the petitioner. After purchase the vendor handed over peaceful vacant possession of the petitioner and the petitioner started living there with her family member. The petitioner resided in the house up to September, 1980. In the meantime, the husband of the petitioner obtained allotment of a quarter from Bangladesh Jute Mills Corporation of which he was an officer and the petitioner sifted to the house by letting out this house on rent to one Abdul Halim. After departure of the said tenant Abdul Halim the petitioner let cut the house to one Kalu Meah contractor who defaulted to pay the rent. Consequently, the petitioner filed Complaint Case No. 48 of 1981 with the Pahartali Ward office of the Chittagong Municipal Corporation. During the pendency of the said case Kalu Meah contractor paid rent to her through the Arbitration Council and the said Arbitration council gave a Judgment on 25-10-1981 in favour of the petitioner. Thereafter the petitioner came to know that the Government declared her house as an Abandoned property. The petitioner filed an application to the Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong. The Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong vide memo No. Ap /186 dated 5-5-1998 informed the petitioner to submit her documents. The petitioner submitted all the relevant documents on 12-5-1983, subsequently the Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong advised her to approach to the Ministry of Works, abandoned properties wing for release of her house. The petitioner applied to the respondent No. 1 who asked her to submit her documents. She filed all her documents on 13-8-1988. Then the Ministry of Works found that the petitioner is the rightful owner, possessor and have interest in the house and released the property from 'Ka list vide Memo No. Sha Kha-9 /IM-37/88 /199 dated 16-5-1989 under serial No. 54 and placed the house to the Commissioner (Settlement) for taking appropriate steps (Annexure-'E' to the Writ Petition). In the meantime, BS Khatian was prepared and the house was recorded in the name of Ministry of Works and the respondent No. 4 took control of the house by evicting the tenant of the petitioner. Consequently, the petitioner applied to the authority to restore possession. The respondent No. 4 advised the petitioner vide Memo No. 939 dated 12-2-1986 to move the Court of Settlement. Consequently, the petitioner filed Case No. 438 of 1992 before the Court of Settlement, Second Court, Dhaka. After hearing the Court of Settlement found that the house has already been released lawfully in. favour of the petitioner by the judgment and order dated 13-3-1006 (Annexure-'F' to the writ petition.) Thereafter the petitioner filed an application to the Commissioner (Settlement) to restore the possession of the property in favour of the petitioner. The Commissioner (Settlement) vide Memo No. AH-84/92/687 dated 28-1-1997 addressed to the Deputy Commissioner/President, allotment Committee recommend restoration of possession of the house in favour of the petitioner (Annexure 'G' to the writ petition). The petitioner repeatedly approached the matter to the respondents to hand over possession of the properties in favour of the petitioner. On 19-10-1999 the petitioner filed a Mutation Case No.189/799-2000 to the Assistant Commissioner (Land). The Assistant Commissioner (Land) by his judgment and order dated 3-1-2000 found that after release of the house by the Ministry of Works handed over possession to the Commissioner on Settlement for the purpose of handing over peaceful possession officially to the petitioner. But the respondent No. 4 most illegally and without any jurisdiction transferred the house to one Abul Kashem instead of handing over possession to the petitioner. He further submits that Added respondent Md Abul Kashem with Malafide intention to grab the property of the petitioner mortgaged to get the property registered in his favour and that on 9-5-1990 deed of transfer was executed by the respondent No. 4, vide Deed No. 1708 which is malafide, illegal, with-out jurisdiction, void, and in operative in the eye of law. He further submits that since the house has been released from the list of Abandoned Property vide Memo No. Sha Kha-9/1M-37/88/199 dated 16-5-1989. The subsequent allotment or subsequent deed of transfer by the respondent No. 4 in favour of Added respondent No. 5 Md Abul Kashem is void malafide, illegal without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. He further submits that all the statements of the respondents has been admitted the facts asserted by the petitioner which amounts to admission of the facts. Moreover, respondent No. 4 had no right to give allotment to added respondent No. 5 on 18-1-1990., After release of the house by the Government on 16-5-1989 from the list of abandoned property in view of Section 12 of the Abandoned buildings (Subsequent possession) Ordinance, 1985 (Ordinance No. 54 of 1986). In support of his contention, he cited the case of Javed Alam (Md) vs Bangladesh 55 DLR 521, the case of Akhtar Hossain vs Bangladesh, represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Works reported in 52 DLR 148, the case of Hashem (Md) vs Bangladesh reported in 43 DLR 159, the case of Wahidul Haque vs Bangladesh 54 DLR 165.
